headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose tariffs that allocate certain grid infrastructure costs to large energy users, aiming to prevent these costs from burdening residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, some utility companies.
news_headline: Virginia Poll: Data Centers Should Pay Full Energy Costs
news_summary: A recent poll found that 89% of registered Virginia voters believe data centers should cover the full cost of new energy infrastructure built for them. This sentiment reflects concerns about rising household electricity bills, with 64% of respondents expressing high concern.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, supplied to these facilities to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, environmental advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Del. Liz Guzman.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates local water authorities to publicly report data center water usage. This aims to provide transparency and better inform the discourse around the industry's water consumption, with data expected to be available on the DEQ website by January 1, 2027.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community advocates, residents near data centers, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul, Sen. Danica A. Roem.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: Siting, Noise Studies
news_summary: Virginia's new law, effective July 1, 2026, mandates site assessments for large data centers to study noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. While it requires studies and utility disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local governments.
